xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4885: Anywhere re-run (PAN-4882): AC-4 pan worker run to an online Fly link fails on the 2.5 s secure-channel budget

plan.title: Anywhere re-run (PAN-4882): AC-4 pan worker run to an online Fly link fails on the 2.5 s secure-channel budget
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: openLinkSocket (src/lib/anywhere/link-client.ts) uses LINK_WAIT_MS (2.5 s) both as the wait for a connecting link and as openChannel's timeoutMs for the handshake to an already-online link. Over the public Fly route (TLS to the Fly edge, the fly-force-instance-id pin, then Noise IK) the open misses 2.5 s often enough that two of three `pan worker run --machine fly-…` starts failed with 'Secure channel to wss://pan-workspaces.fly.dev/ws/link?fly-instance=… did not open within 2500 ms' while the link was online with a fresh heartbeat.
narratives.Proposal: Add export const LINK_OPEN_MS = 10_000 to link-client.ts and pass it as openChannel's timeoutMs in openLinkSocket; keep LINK_WAIT_MS (2.5 s) as the connecting wait only. Rewrite the module header so it states both budgets. Prove both budgets with a new fake-timer test file that mocks openChannel and delegates to the real withDeadline. Document the two budgets in docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md and add a troubleshooting bullet to configuration/linked-machines.mdx. Full detail, before/after snippets and named tests in .pan/drafts/PAN-4885.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No retry of a failed channel open; the existing GET/HEAD/OPTIONS stale-channel resend stays unchanged.
- No change to LINK_WAIT_MS or to the connecting-wait behavior (waitOnline still gets 2.5 s; afterWait message unchanged).
- No change to the link supervisor's 2.5 s probe budget in src/dashboard/server/services/link-supervisor.ts.
- No change inside packages/anywhere-channel/ (DEFAULT_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, withDeadline, error text).
- No change to Fly routing (fly-force-instance-id, FLY_INSTANCE_PARAM) or WORK_DOOR_TIMEOUT_MS.
- No change to fleet callers' own 2.5 s AbortSignal bounds (fleet-awareness, fleet-usage, machines-fleet).
- No edits to src/lib/anywhere/__tests__/link-client.test.ts and no edit to the dated 2026-11-03 entry in docs/ANYWHERE-RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md.
- No live Fly re-run is required to merge.

autoDecisions.summary: Chose a separate, larger open budget (LINK_OPEN_MS = 10 s) for an online link over one retry of the open.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue offered both without a default. The evidence shows two consecutive failures 22 s apart, then a success: a slow window lasting tens of seconds. A retry fired 2.5 s into the same window would likely fail again; a longer budget lets the slow open finish. 10 s equals the channel package's own DEFAULT_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS and fits inside the 30 s WORK_DOOR_TIMEOUT_MS.

autoDecisions.summary: LINK_OPEN_MS is a literal in link-client.ts, not an import of DEFAULT_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is a policy of the link client; importing the package default would move it silently if the package changes.

autoDecisions.summary: Callers without a signal (ws-linked, port-forwards) now wait up to 10 s on an online-but-dead link.
autoDecisions.rationale: Accepted tradeoff: the supervisor marks such a link offline within 20 s, after which calls fail at once; callers needing a shorter bound already pass a signal.

items.title: Add LINK_OPEN_MS (10 s) and pass it as openLinkSocket's channel-open timeout

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-1 exactly. In src/lib/anywhere/link-client.ts: (1) rewrite the module header lines 14-17 to the 'After' text in the PRD (states LINK_WAIT_MS for the connecting wait and LINK_OPEN_MS for the open, cites PAN-4885, says callers needing a shorter bound pass a signal); (2) after `export const LINK_WAIT_MS = 2_500;` add the documented `export const LINK_OPEN_MS = 10_000;`; (3) in openLinkSocket change `timeoutMs: LINK_WAIT_MS,` to `timeoutMs: LINK_OPEN_MS,`; (4) update the openLinkSocket doc comment as in the PRD. Do not touch waitOnline(…, LINK_WAIT_MS) calls, afterWait, or linkFetch/linkForward comments about the 2.5 s connecting wait. No change in packages/anywhere-channel/.

items.title: Given src/lib/anywhere/link-client.ts, when grepped, then `timeoutMs: LINK_OPEN_MS` appears once inside openLinkSocket, `timeoutMs: LINK_WAIT_MS` returns no match, and both `export const LINK_OPEN_MS = 10_000;` and `export const LINK_WAIT_MS = 2_500;` exist

Given the module header of link-client.ts, when read, then it no longer contains 'No user-facing call waits more than 2.5 s' and names both LINK_WAIT_MS (connecting wait) and LINK_OPEN_MS (open budget)
Given the change, when `npm run typecheck` runs, then it exits 0 and `git diff --stat origin/main -- packages/anywhere-channel` produces no output
Fake-timer tests proving the 10 s open budget and the 2.5 s connecting wait

expected_outputs: link-open-budget.test.ts passes with its five named tests

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-2. Create src/lib/anywhere/__tests__/link-open-budget.test.ts. vi.mock('../channel/open.js') keeping the original exports but replacing openChannel with vi.fn(). Use vi.useFakeTimers() in beforeEach and vi.useRealTimers() + mockReset + _resetLinkClientForTests() in afterEach. For behavioral cases make the mock call the real withDeadline from '@overdeck/anywhere-channel' with a run that resolves a duplexPair end after N ms via setTimeout, so the deadline decides under fake timers with no real I/O. Write the five named tests from the PRD: (1) online link → openChannel called with timeoutMs LINK_OPEN_MS (and LINK_OPEN_MS===10_000, LINK_WAIT_MS===2_500); (2) a 3 s open resolves; (3) an open pending at LINK_OPEN_MS rejects with ChannelOpenError code 'timeout' and message ending 'did not open within 10000 ms' (attach the rejection handler before advancing timers); (4) connecting link: waitOnline receives LINK_WAIT_MS and the open receives LINK_OPEN_MS; waitOnline false → LinkUnavailableError 'machine-unreachable' and openChannel never called; (5) offline link → 'machine-offline', openChannel never called. Do not edit link-client.test.ts. No source-file grepping, no skipIf/.only, no real net/ws sockets.

items.title: Given an online link whose mocked open takes 3 000 ms under fake timers, when openLinkSocket runs and timers advance 3 000 ms, then the promise resolves with the channel
Given an online link whose open never completes, when timers advance LINK_OPEN_MS, then openLinkSocket rejects with ChannelOpenError code 'timeout' and a message ending 'did not open within 10000 ms'

Given a connecting link, when openLinkSocket runs, then waitOnline receives LINK_WAIT_MS and, if it returns false, the call rejects with LinkUnavailableError 'machine-unreachable' without calling openChannel; if it returns true, openChannel receives timeoutMs LINK_OPEN_MS

Given the new file and the unchanged link-client.test.ts, when `npx vitest run src/lib/anywhere/__tests__/link-open-budget.test.ts src/lib/anywhere/__tests__/link-client.test.ts` runs, then both files pass and the new file uses vi.useFakeTimers with no real net or ws socket
Document the connecting wait vs open budget in the architecture doc and linked-machines troubleshooting
